name: Satellite sea colour (algae)
summary: Chlorophyll-a in the sea off Larnaka, Limassol and Paphos from a satellite colour sensor (VIIRS): more green = more algae/plankton. Coastal cities only. Days old; clouds leave gaps.
tagline: Algae from space · coastal cities only

el.name: Χρώμα θάλασσας από δορυφόρο (φύκια)
el.summary: Χλωροφύλλη-a στη θάλασσα ανοιχτά της Λάρνακας, της Λεμεσού και της Πάφου από δορυφορικό αισθητήρα χρώματος (VIIRS): περισσότερο πράσινο = περισσότερα φύκια/πλαγκτόν. Μόνο παράκτιες πόλεις. Έχει καθυστέρηση ημερών· τα σύννεφα αφήνουν κενά.
el.tagline: Φύκια από δορυφόρο · μόνο παράκτιες πόλεις

coverage.area: Sea off Larnaka, Limassol and Paphos (not Lefkosia)

update.note: Science-quality maps arrive 11 to 15 days late. Clouds leave holes.

variables.note: Estimated from the colour of the sea (the provider's default recipe)

quality.uncertainty: Studies found standard global colour recipes very uncertain in the Mediterranean (about 100%) and worse near coasts. Use it for patterns and change, not exact numbers.
known_issues: A satellite sees only the colour of the top few metres, and only through clear sky. We use the newest clear view of the last 7 days and say its date.
Science-quality maps are about 11 to 15 days old: the value is never today's.
Near the coast, shallow sand, dust in the air and land in the pixel can make the value too high. A pixel is about 4 km wide.
Offshore, the eastern Mediterranean is low in algae, so values are small and easy to over-read.

use_for: Where the sea near a coastal city looks greener (more algae)
Teaching how the colour of the sea shows life in it
not_for: Water quality or whether it is safe to swim

notes: Read from the NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP, dataset nesdisVHNSQchlaDaily (chlor_a, mg m^-3, 4 km), newest 7 daily maps in a small box per city. Same-server chlorophyll datasets that have stopped are not used (noaacwNPPN20VIIRSchlociDaily, noaacwN20VIIRSchlaWeekly, nesdisVHNSQchlaWeekly, erdVH3chla8day).
